Think of a wheel with a single spoke (figure A in the below link)

spokes

As weight is placed on the hub that weight is transferred to the top of the rim via that single spoke. The force pulling down from the top of the rim is then transferred around the rim to the ground. With one spoke though, unless the rim was built very strongly (and very heavily), the rim would want to deform under under the weight (figure B). To avoid this, we need to add more spokes that counter the outward forces on the sides of the rim and keep the rim in shape. While the spokes leading to the top half of the wheel are carrying more weight, every spoke around the hub is still in tension, otherwise the rim would deform and fail.
